title: Superpowers and Emerging Powers
welcome_lead: From Washington and Beijing to Brasília and New Delhi — survey the shifting hierarchy of world power.
meta_desc: Geography HL Adventure: superpowers, emerging powers and shifting global influence.
final_note: You have surveyed the multipolar world taking shape. Geographies of power are dynamic.

concepts.def: State exerting comprehensive global influence across military, economic, technological and cultural domains.
Dominant state setting norms and structures within an international system.
Group of major emerging economies (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, expanded 2024).
Group of seven major advanced economies meeting annually.
Forum of 19 countries plus the European Union covering most of world GDP.
Halford Mackinder's 1904 thesis that control of the Eurasian 'heartland' confers global power.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Cold War's bipolar order gave way after 1991 to perceived US 'unipolarity'. The rise of China — second largest economy, leading in manufacturing and increasingly in technology — alongside India, Russia, Brazil and middle powers like Turkey is producing a more multipolar landscape.

The G7 represents advanced HICs; the G20 includes the largest emerging economies; BRICS expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE. These forums illustrate both cooperation and rivalry, and the diffusion of agenda-setting power.

Classical geopolitics (Mackinder's heartland, Mahan's sea power) still informs strategy. Newer frameworks emphasise networks, technology and economic interdependence. Belt and Road, the Indo-Pacific concept and EU strategic autonomy all illustrate competing visions of geopolitical organisation.
